text:
Marathon Petroleum ticked up 0.66% today to $393.52, a modest gain in what has been a rough two weeks of selling. The move comes as U.S. crude oil sits at $96.41 per barrel—down sharply this week after Iran-U.S. talks at the U.N. reduced near-term conflict fears—but refineries are running hot at 94% capacity with relatively tight inventory levels, which supports refining margins and the company's core business.

The broader picture is a tug-of-war: geopolitical risk to oil supply (ongoing Iran tensions, Trump's reported plan for renewed bombing after midterms) is putting a floor under crude prices and keeping refiners busy, but the mere possibility of diplomacy earlier this week knocked nearly 8% off oil prices and dragged the stock down from $424 to under $390. Today's small rebound likely reflects a stabilization in that tension, though the stock remains well off its recent highs as investors weigh whether oil prices can hold.
